patches.old: People in high-arousal situations tend to label their emotions based on context
patches.new: Different emotions are accompanied by somewhat different patterns of autonomic activity

patches.old: Choice A is a criticism better directed at James-Lange but actually describes a finding used to support Schachter-Singer.
patches.new: Choice A is not a criticism at all: emotion-specific autonomic patterns are exactly what James-Lange predicts, and evidence for them supports the theory rather than undermining it.

visual.title: The experiment that made the two-factor case
visual.alt: A table of the Schachter and Singer design showing uninformed, misinformed and informed epinephrine groups and a saline group crossed with euphoric and angry confederates, with the resulting emotions; a four-step chain illustrating excitation transfer on Dutton and Aron's suspension bridge; and Lazarus's primary appraisal categories of irrelevant, benign-positive, harm, threat and challenge beside secondary appraisal of coping options and reappraisal.
visual.caption: Only one thing differs down the epinephrine rows: whether the person already has an explanation for the pounding heart. That alone decides the emotion.
